concept: Kamino Multiply and eMode or elevation groups

claims.text: A Kamino elevation group (eMode) is a curator-defined cluster of correlated assets (stablecoins, LSTs with their underlying SOL, wrapped assets with natives). A user joins voluntarily; the program then applies the group's LTV and liquidation threshold in place of per-reserve defaults. Leaving the group, or borrowing an asset outside it, restores the per-reserve defaults. (high confidence)

A market supports at most 32 elevation groups (IDs 1-32; 0 means no group). Per the docs, a single reserve can opt into up to 20 groups, and group parameters only apply to reserves that list the group ID in their own elevation_groups array. (medium confidence)

Group configuration is not exposed through the REST API; a curator sets it through the SDK or Kamino CLI. Setting allow_new_loans to 0 pauses new borrows in a group while existing positions keep their relaxed parameters and can still repay and exit. (low confidence)

Kamino's eMode is the elevation group. One lending market stores up to 32 groups (ids 1-32; id 0 means no group). Each group sets ltv_pct, liquidation_threshold_pct, max_liquidation_bonus_bps, allow_new_loans, max_reserves_as_collateral and exactly one debt_reserve. (high confidence)

Kamino prices LSTs (JitoSOL, mSOL, bSOL) by stake rate (SOL_staked / LST_minted) read from the on-chain stake pool account, not by DEX price, so a temporary market depeg neither changes position health nor triggers liquidation. The same design exposes positions to genuine backing impairment such as a staking-protocol exploit, which lowers the stake rate. (high confidence)

The SDK's default Multiply open builder orders the transaction: refresh oracles; create or wrap token accounts; flash-borrow the collateral token from the collateral reserve; deposit; request the elevation group between deposit and borrow; refresh reserves and obligation; borrow the debt token; swap debt to collateral; flash-repay. A second builder flash-borrows the debt token first (swap, then deposit and borrow, then repay). Kamino's docs give a simplified seven-step order with the swap before the deposit. Because the default flash loan comes from the collateral reserve, it needs unborrowed collateral-token liquidity there. (medium confidence)

Multiply opens, adjusts and closes a leveraged position in one atomic transaction built on a klend flash loan (0.001% fee on each open, adjust or close). The docs list the open sequence as flash-borrow, swap through Kamino Swap, deposit collateral, borrow the debt asset, repay the flash loan. The SDK builds two variants: flash-borrow the collateral token (deposit and borrow, which carries the elevation-group request, then swap debt to collateral, then repay) or flash-borrow the debt token (swap first, then deposit and borrow). If any step fails, the whole transaction reverts. (high confidence)

Kamino-run auto-deleverage is a last-resort tool initiated by its Risk Council under extreme systemic stress: positions get a 72-hour warning, it targets the largest leveraged positions, and Kamino says it has never been triggered. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Higher eMode LTVs shrink the gap between operating LTV and the liquidation threshold, so at near-max leverage a modest adverse move in the yield spread (staking yield minus SOL borrow rate) matters more. Kamino names sustained borrow rate above LST yield, and LST smart-contract exploits, as the main liquidation paths for SOL-LST Multiply rather than SOL price moves. (medium confidence)

Kamino publishes a checklist rather than a formula. Before enabling a group, curators should confirm member correlation (test depeg and divergence history), pick the single most liquid or most wanted debt_reserve, cap max_reserves_as_collateral, tighten max_liquidation_bonus_bps to realistic correlated-asset slippage, set per-collateral group borrow limits, and set disable_usage_as_coll_outside_emode to 1 for LSTs (often 0 for stables). Reference ranges are 88-92% LTV and 90-95% threshold for LSTs against their underlying, and 90-95% and 92-97% for stables-only groups. (medium confidence)

Kamino prices SOL LSTs by stake rate (SOL staked / LST minted), read from the stake pool account, not by DEX price. A market discount, such as JitoSOL at 0.95 SOL against a 1.05 SOL stake rate, does not change a Multiply position's LTV. A real loss of backing (exploit, slashing) lowers the stake rate and does change it. Kamino says this is why market depegs have not liquidated LST Multiply positions. (medium confidence)
